D001 — Job Center Design System v1

Follow project governance documents.

Documentation only. Do not modify plugin code, routes, templates, schema, styles, or behavior.

Goal

Create the canonical visual and interaction specification for the Teachers.Net Job Center.

This document will govern future UX audits, mockups, implementation tickets, and QA.

Authoritative inputs

- docs/job-center/canonical-v1-contract.md
- docs/job-center/employer-ux-v1.md
- current implementation map and project cursor
- UA001–UA003
- docs/design-system-v1.md
- approved Job Center design references available in the repository

Reference control

Before writing the specification:

1. Inventory available Job Center mockups and visual references.
2. Distinguish approved/current references from drafts, experiments, and superseded work.
3. Do not infer approval from filename, recency, or current implementation.
4. Where no approved reference exists, document the requirement as unresolved rather than inventing a design.
5. The current implementation is evidence, not the visual authority.

Deliverable

Create:

docs/job-center/job-center-design-system-v1.md

Include:

1. Purpose and authority
2. Source hierarchy and conflict rules
3. Design principles
4. Page canvas, grid, gutters, and responsive behavior
5. Typography hierarchy
6. Color and interface states
7. Navigation, breadcrumb, hero, and footer rules
8. Buttons, links, forms, selectors, chips, notices, and status indicators
9. Search interaction model
10. Canonical job-listing composition
11. Job-detail presentation principles
12. Employer interface principles
13. Right-rail structure
14. Advertising placements and reserved dimensions
15. Pagination and result-count treatment
16. Icons, including Save/heart behavior
17. Accessibility and focus requirements
18. Approved-reference index
19. Unresolved design needs
20. Versioning and supersession rules

Required rules

- Entire desktop shell uses a centered 1200px maximum-width canvas.
- Navbar and footer remain constrained to the page canvas.
- Navbar is white.
- Footer is the standard dark Teachers.Net blue.
- Listing presentation is a two-zone professional directory entry, not a table.
- Taxonomy metadata remains grouped in the narrative block.
- Salary, distance, and Save occupy the compact secondary block.
- Search uses progressive disclosure.
- Advertising is treated as an intentional layout component.
- Employer UX must conform to Employer UX V1.
- Approved references outrank legacy implementation.
- Unresolved screens must remain explicitly unresolved.

Also create a concise reference inventory within the document showing, for each known visual artifact:

- identifier or filename
- represented screen/component
- status: Approved / Draft / Superseded / Unclassified
- authority notes
- related future UX Atlas entry

Do not

- redesign screens
- generate mockups
- implement CSS
- silently promote uncertain references to Approved
- describe unsupported functionality as implemented
- create implementation tickets

Verification

- documentation only
- Jobs plugin unchanged
- git diff --check clean

Commit

DOC001 — Engineering Handoff v2

Follow project governance documents.

Documentation only.

Do not modify plugin code, routes, templates, schema, styles, or product behavior.

Goal

Update the Engineering Director workflow, supporting documentation, and Google Drive handoff process to reflect the current project governance model.

The objective is to minimize future AI quota consumption while ensuring that every new ChatGPT engineering session begins from authoritative project state rather than conversational memory.

Background

Recent testing demonstrated that ChatGPT project memory successfully recalls broad historical context but does not reliably maintain current engineering state, ticket sequencing, approved design authority, or active governance documents.

The Engineering Handoff therefore remains the authoritative continuity mechanism between Codex and new ChatGPT sessions.

Objectives

1. Review all existing handoff documentation.
2. Remove obsolete or duplicated guidance.
3. Update the Engineering Director Playbook where appropriate.
4. Update all local handoff templates.
5. Update the Google Drive Engineering Handoff document.
6. Update the standard startup prompt used for new ChatGPT sessions.
7. Keep prompts concise and governance-driven to reduce token consumption.

Engineering Handoff v2 Requirements

The Handoff shall become an operational state document rather than a historical summary.

Every handoff shall answer only:

1. Current Phase
2. Current Ticket
3. Last Completed Milestone
4. Next Five Planned Tickets
5. Current Blockers
6. Recently Adopted Governance Documents
7. Recently Approved Product Decisions
8. Recently Approved Visual References
9. Active Design Authority
10. Immediate Engineering Priorities

The handoff shall NOT:

- summarize project history
- restate settled architecture
- duplicate permanent governance
- duplicate Design System content
- duplicate Product Contract content
- repeat implementation details already preserved elsewhere

Startup Procedure

Revise the standard startup instructions so that new ChatGPT sessions read:

- Engineering Director Playbook
- Current Engineering Handoff

Only when needed should additional governance documents be consulted, including:

- Current Project Cursor
- Canonical Product Contract
- Employer UX V1
- Job Center Design System v1
- Visual Manifest

The startup prompt shall instruct ChatGPT to:

- adopt the current engineering state
- report only:
  - current phase
  - current ticket
  - last completed milestone
  - next five planned tickets
  - current blockers

It shall not summarize the governance documents.

Quota Optimization

Revise the workflow to minimize AI compute by:

- referencing governance instead of repeating it
- treating permanent documents as stable
- making the Engineering Handoff delta-oriented
- avoiding historical recap
- keeping implementation tickets narrowly scoped
- using one objective per ticket
- requiring Codex to stop at defined ticket boundaries

Review Existing Documents

Inspect and update, where appropriate:

- Engineering Director Playbook
- Codex Direction Manual
- Current Project Cursor
- Engineering Handoff template
- Google Drive Engineering Handoff document
- any local documentation referencing the previous handoff procedure

Deliverables

Provide:

- updated local documentation
- updated Google Drive handoff document
- updated startup prompt
- concise summary of workflow changes

Verification

- documentation only
- Jobs plugin unchanged
- git diff --check clean

DOC002 — Search & Discovery Interaction Suite v1

Follow project governance documents.

Documentation only.

Do not modify plugin code, templates, routes, schema, styles, behavior, or approved visual artifacts.

Goal

Recognize completion of the governed Search & Discovery interaction suite and update project documentation so future implementation and audit work can reference the suite as a coherent product milestone rather than a collection of unrelated mockups.

Purpose

The Job Finder now has approved visual references covering the complete first-touch interaction sequence.

DOC005 — JC-030 Job Detail Product Definition

Follow project governance documents.

Documentation only.

Do not modify plugin code, templates, routes, schema, styles, behavior, approved visual artifacts, or the Visual Manifest.

## Goal

Create the canonical product definition for:

JC-030 — Job Detail

This ticket defines product truth only.

It must not define layout, visual hierarchy, component placement, responsive behavior, or implementation.

## Authoritative Inputs

Consult only as needed:

* Engineering Director Playbook
* Job Center Engineering Handoff
* Project Cursor
* Canonical V1 Contract
* Job Center UX Atlas v1
* approved Search & Discovery Interaction Suite references:

  * JC-010
  * JC-014
  * JC-015
  * JC-011
* current product, UX, design-system, roadmap, and implementation documents where directly relevant

Treat approved documents and artifacts as authority.

Do not reopen or reinterpret settled Search & Discovery behavior.

## Required Definition

Define the following for JC-030:

### Purpose

Convert an interested teacher into an applicant.

### Primary Goal

Present complete job information with maximum clarity and trust while maximizing application conversion.

### Product Role

Define:

* where Job Detail sits in the governed job-seeker journey
* what user need it satisfies
* what responsibility belongs to Job Detail
* what responsibility belongs to adjacent screens or systems

### Primary User

Identify the primary user and relevant authenticated or unauthenticated conditions already supported by governed product decisions.

Do not invent new user classes.

### User Objectives

Define the essential user outcomes Job Detail must support.

### Required Information

Identify the job information that must be available to satisfy the product purpose.

Describe information requirements only.

Do not prescribe layout, order, grouping, visual treatment, or component structure.

### Supported Actions

Identify the product-level actions available from Job Detail.

Distinguish clearly between:

* primary conversion action
* secondary user actions
* navigation actions
* authenticated-only actions, where already governed

Do not define UI controls or interaction design.

### Trust Requirements

Define the product information or conditions necessary for the page to establish confidence in:

* the job
* the employer
* application expectations
* listing freshness or status

Do not invent verification systems or new functionality.

### States and Conditions

Identify product states that later UX work must account for, including only states supported by current product truth.

Examples may include authentication, job availability, application method, saved state, or employer/listing conditions where already governed.

Do not specify their visual or interaction treatment.

### Dependencies

Identify approved upstream inputs and downstream work that depends on this definition.

### Success Criteria

Define concise product-level success criteria.

Avoid analytics implementation detail unless existing governance already establishes it.

### Explicitly Out of Scope

State that this definition does not govern:

* layout
* visual hierarchy
* typography
* spacing
* component selection
* responsive adaptation
* technical architecture
* implementation
* speculative future features

## Deliverable

Create:

docs/job-center/jc-030-job-detail-product-definition.md

Keep the document concise, stable, implementation-independent, and suitable as authority for later UX specification and visual-governance work.

* Job Center UX Atlas v1
* Project Cursor
* Engineering Handoff
* roadmap

Do not duplicate the full product definition elsewhere.

## Status Handling

JC-030 remains:

Placeholder

It does not create approved UX, visual, responsive, or implementation authority.

Do not change JC-030 to Approved in the Visual Manifest.

* documentation only
* Jobs plugin unchanged
* approved artifacts unchanged
* Visual Manifest unchanged unless a strictly necessary textual reference is explicitly justified
* no layout, visual hierarchy, or implementation decisions were introduced
* `git diff --check` clean
* unrelated dirty or untracked files untouched

## Commit

Commit only the completed and verified documentation work.

DOC005 define JC-030 Job Detail product truth

## Stop Boundary

Stop after:

* creating the product-definition document
* adding only necessary concise cross-references
* completing verification
* committing the work

Do not begin UX specification, mockup generation, visual governance, implementation audit, or application-code changes.

Text:
For the Teachers.Net Job Center work, I recommend **Power / GPT-5.6 Sol with Medium reasoning** as the normal default.

That fits our mixture of repository inspection, product/UX judgment, visual governance, implementation, verification, and careful documentation. OpenAI describes Sol as the choice for complex, open-ended, high-value work; Medium balances depth and speed. [Model selection documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/models)

Adjust by task:

- **High reasoning:** visual approvals, architecture decisions, difficult debugging, release-readiness audits, and cross-document reconciliation.
- **Medium reasoning:** normal implementation tickets, documentation updates, verification, and Git work.
- **Light reasoning:** narrowly mechanical edits with exact instructions.
- **Max:** only for unusually difficult, consequential analysis.
- **Ultra:** generally unnecessary here. Our work is sequential and governance-sensitive, and this repository disallows subagent delegation unless explicitly requested.
- **Fast mode:** optional when latency matters, but not my default because it consumes substantially more credits.

For durable local configuration, I’d use:

```toml
model = "gpt-5.6"
model_reasoning_effort = "medium"
approval_policy = "on-request"
sandbox_mode = "workspace-write"
web_search = "cached"
```

For DDEV/Docker operations that cannot run inside `workspace-write`, temporarily grant broader access for that operation instead of making unrestricted access the permanent default. Project-specific configuration belongs in `.codex/config.toml`; personal defaults belong in `~/.codex/config.toml`. [Configuration basics](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-basic)

My practical recommendation for this thread is: **stay on GPT-5.6 Sol, Medium**, switch to **High** for the upcoming JC-010 mobile candidate review, and reserve Max for genuinely difficult decisions. Continue using `AGENTS.md`, the Project Cursor, and Engineering Handoff as the durable context layer; that is more important for consistency than increasing reasoning on every task. [Codex best practices](https://learn.chatgpt.com/guides/best-practices)

CODEX-019f605b-A0011
Role: ASSISTANT
Source line: 129
Timestamp: 2026-07-14T11:30:04.507Z

Text:
Not exactly.

- **Cheaper:** Yes. API pricing for Terra is exactly half of Sol: **$2.50 input / $15 output per million tokens**, versus **$5 / $30** for Sol. GPT-5.5 is also $5/$30. [Terra details](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-terra) and [Sol details](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-sol)
- **Faster:** Possibly in practical use, but OpenAI officially labels both Terra and Sol as **“Fast”** and does not publish a precise relative latency ratio.
- **Comparable to GPT-5.5:** Terra can replace GPT-5.5 for much routine coding and tool work, but it is not positioned as a capability-equivalent successor. OpenAI says Terra roughly corresponds to the earlier **mini tier**. Sol corresponds to the earlier unsuffixed flagship tier, making **Sol the closer conceptual successor to GPT-5.5**.

For our project:

- Use **Terra Medium/High** for clear implementation tickets, tests, Git work, and routine documentation.
- Use **Sol Medium/High** for visual approval, architecture, ambiguous debugging, release decisions, and reconciling several governance documents.

A good cost-conscious default would be **Terra Medium**, switching to **Sol High** for the consequential Job Center decisions. For the upcoming JC-010 visual-authority review, I would choose Sol.

Follow the Engineering Director Playbook and current Job Center governance.

Goal

Approved artifacts

1. LO-1st-touch-w-hamburger-overlay.png
2. LI-1st-touch-w-hamburger-overlay.png

Approval scope

These artifacts govern only the mobile navigation drawer component and its presentation.

The approval includes:

- drawer structure
- logo/header
- close control
- section hierarchy
- typography
- spacing rhythm
- icon treatment
- navigation row composition
- footer treatment
- social row
- logged-out acquisition panel
- logged-in profile header
- logout presentation
- overlay behavior and visual treatment

This approval does NOT independently approve any underlying page, responsive layout, tablet layout, or implementation.

Component authority

- JC-010
- JC-011
- JC-014
- JC-015
- JC-030

unless a future screen explicitly documents an approved exception.

1. Copy both approved rasters into:

2. Add new manifest entries for the mobile navigation drawer component:

   - Logged In

3. Update the Approved Mockup Library README.

5. Update the Project Cursor.

- redesign either drawer

- establish tablet authority

- modify JC-010, JC-011, JC-014, JC-015, or JC-030 beyond referencing the shared drawer component

Verification

- Verify the exact approved source rasters were used.

- Run `git diff --check`.

Git

Commit only this governance work.

DOC006 approve mobile navigation drawer authority

Push to origin.

Report only:

- approved filenames
- SHA-256 values
- files changed
- commit
- push

CODEX-019f605b-A0048
Role: ASSISTANT
Source line: 643
Timestamp: 2026-07-14T12:47:31.913Z

Text:
Audit complete — 6 findings.

1. **Major — Advertisement reservation**  
   **Reason:** The labelled `728 × 90` leaderboard is rendered as a shallow, distorted strip in the main column, rather than retaining its intrinsic proportion where the tablet content inset can accommodate it.  
   **Recommendation:** Place this reservation across the tablet content inset after pagination and reserve the true 728:90 proportion; do not compress it to the listing-column width.

2. **Major — Right rail reading flow and order**  
   **Reason:** The portrait render retains the rail beside results and displays Account → Browse → Popular Searches → Hiring → Career Chatboards. The responsive decision calls for the support region after results, pagination, and leaderboard, ordered Account → Browse → Employer → Advertisement → Community.  
   **Recommendation:** At the tablet reflow boundary, move the existing rail cards into that prescribed support-flow position and order; retain the approved card designs and content.

3. **Minor — Sort control**  
   **Reason:** The visible “Most Recent” control is appreciably shorter than the 36px shared control height, making it less comfortable for touch than adjacent search controls.  
   **Recommendation:** Increase only the sort select’s rendered control box to the shared 36px minimum, preserving its current label and placement.

4. **Minor — Listing metadata and chips**  
   **Reason:** Employer/location text and taxonomy chips are visibly small relative to the tablet canvas, reducing scan readability despite otherwise strong listing hierarchy.  
   **Recommendation:** Increase those two localized text treatments by one type step and retain the current title → identity → chips → summary order.

5. **Observation — Save controls**  
   **Reason:** The heart glyphs are visually compact; the raster cannot confirm whether each has a compliant interactive hit area.  
   **Recommendation:** Ensure each heart is wrapped in a separate control meeting the minimum target requirement, with a preferred approximately 44px quiet hit area, without enlarging the visible glyph.

6. **Minor — Footer small text density**  
   **Reason:** Footer link, copyright, and supporting text are dense and small for portrait-tablet reading, particularly in the multi-column region.  
   **Recommendation:** Increase footer secondary/link text and line spacing one step while preserving the existing column organization and newsletter placement.

Text:
1. **Major — Leaderboard reservation**  
   The labelled `728 × 90` leaderboard is visibly compressed to a shallow main-column strip. At this tablet width, the content inset can accommodate an intrinsic 728:90 reservation; the rendered proportion does not meet the responsive advertising rule.

2. **Major — Right-rail advertisement reservation**  
   The right-rail placeholder labelled `300 × 250` is visibly taller than its declared 1.2:1 proportion. The responsive decision requires this placement to retain its intrinsic reservation.

3. **Major — Distance selector state**  
   The search form displays an apparently available `25 miles` selector while the Location field is empty. JC-010 requires distance to be hidden or disabled until a valid location/origin exists.

4. **Minor — Sort and pagination touch targets**  
   The visible `Most Recent` control and individual pagination buttons appear below the shared 36px control height and below the preferred approximately 44px touch target. The raster does not demonstrate a larger invisible hit area.

5. **Minor — Save-heart hit area cannot be evidenced**  
   The visible hearts correctly remain small and light, but the raster provides no evidence of the required larger interactive target. This must be verified in implementation without enlarging the glyph.

6. **Minor — Footer small-text readability**  
   Footer supporting text, link labels, and copyright remain materially smaller than primary body text in the long portrait composition, creating a readability risk at tablet viewing distance and zoom.

7. **Observation — Responsive rail transition remains unresolved**  
   The rail is still presented beside results and its visible sequence is Account → Browse → Popular Searches → Employer → Community → Advertisement. The governed stacked support order differs, so this candidate does not yet establish the later responsive transition behavior.

8. **Observation — Output viewport fidelity**  
   The saved candidate is 848px wide rather than the intended 1024px tablet width. It can serve as a visual candidate, but it does not by itself verify 1024px implementation spacing, target sizes, or breakpoint behavior.

DOC010 – Codify Responsive Design Principles v1

Follow the Engineering Director Playbook and current Job Center governance.

Goal

Capture the responsive design principles established during JC-010 so future responsive work inherits the same philosophy without rediscovering it.

This is a documentation-only governance ticket.

Do not modify any approved design.

Do not modify implementation.

Do not modify visual authorities.

Update only:

- docs/job-center/job-center-responsive-decisions-v1.md

If appropriate, add brief cross-references in:

- Job Center Design System v1
- Job Center UX Atlas

Required additions

Create a new section:

Portrait Tablet Principles

Document the following principles:

• Desktop governs product truth.

• Mobile governs presentation.

• Tablet preserves desktop information architecture while adopting mobile reading comfort.

• Preserve hierarchy before preserving density.

• Extend vertically before compressing typography.

• Typography should favor comfortable sustained reading over maximum information density.

• Preserve established page identity across responsive adaptations.

• Right-rail support content may remain visible on portrait tablet where it improves first-view usability.

• Responsive work should adapt approved authorities rather than redesign them.

• Once a responsive authority reaches convergence, future work enters Patch Mode.

Create a second section:

Responsive Workflow

Document:

Desktop Authority
        ↓
Tablet Authority
        ↓
Mobile Authority
        ↓
Patch Mode
        ↓
Browser Implementation
        ↓
Browser QA
        ↓
Production Authority

Do NOT

- create new responsive requirements
- redefine breakpoints
- alter approved authorities
- redesign any screen
- modify implementation guidance beyond documenting the established workflow

Verification

Verify:

- no conflicts with the Design System
- no conflicts with the Visual Manifest
- responsive decisions remain internally consistent

Run:

git diff --check

Git

Commit:

DOC010 codify responsive design principles

Push to origin.

Report only:

- sections added
- files changed
- commit
- push

Follow the Engineering Director Playbook and current Job Center governance.

Goal

Determine exactly how the approved JC-011 desktop authority should inherit the established JC-010 tablet and mobile responsive language.

This is a read-only review.

Do not generate images.

2. Regions that inherit with only a localized content/state substitution.
3. Regions unique to JC-011 that require a new responsive decision.
4. Any conflict between JC-011 desktop content and the current responsive decisions.
5. Any product truth that must remain sourced from JC-011 desktop rather than JC-010.

Review these regions specifically:

- navbar and shell
- breadcrumb and heading
- active search controls
- applied-filter chips
- search-summary/results heading
- sort control
- listing composition
- result count and pagination
- right rail/support content
- advertising reservations
- footer
- mobile drawer relationship

Deliverable

Return one concise matrix:

| Region | Tablet treatment | Mobile treatment | Inherited from JC-010? | New decision required? | Notes |

Then provide:

- inherited regions
- unique JC-011 responsive deltas
- blockers, if any
- recommended scope for JC011-R002

Constraints

- Treat JC-011 desktop as product/content authority for the refined-results state.
- Treat approved JC-010 tablet and mobile artifacts as presentation authority.
- Preserve ten jobs per governed page.
- Do not propose alternative layouts unless a genuine conflict prevents inheritance.
- Do not invent new features or V2 behavior.
- Maximum twelve findings or responsive deltas.

Stop after the review.

Text:
| Region | Tablet treatment | Mobile treatment | Inherited from JC-010? | New decision required? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Navbar and shell | Preserve JC-010 tablet constrained shell and desktop-style nav. | Use JC-010 mobile compact bar and approved logged-out drawer. | Yes | No | JC-011 keeps its refined-results content state. |
| Breadcrumb and heading | Preserve breadcrumb and heading placement; substitute `Search Results (42)`. | Use JC-010 mobile’s compact, breadcrumb-free heading treatment. | Yes | No | The refined-results context remains visible through the results count. |
| Active search controls | Retain tablet search composition with JC-011’s populated keyword, location, distance, and Hide filters state. | Retain JC-010 stacked control order with populated values. | Yes, localized state | No | Distance remains valid because JC-011 has a location. |
| Expanded filters and applied chips | Preserve desktop filter content and chips near the search context. | Basic search stack inherits, but the expanded filter panel’s exact disclosure/scroll treatment is unapproved. | Partial | Yes | Chips remain removable state summaries, not taxonomy chips. |
| Search summary, result count, and sort | Use the JC-010 tablet visual hierarchy with `42 jobs found` and the JC-011 sort state. | Use the JC-010 mobile results hierarchy and compact sort treatment. | Yes, localized content | No | Sort and pagination retain comfortable interaction targets. |
| Listing composition | Preserve ten narrative-first listings, secondary salary/distance grouping, and Save-heart styling. | Use JC-010 mobile narrative stacking for the ten JC-011 listings. | Yes, localized content | No | Listing titles, employer/location, summaries, salaries, and supported distance are JC-011 product truth. |
| Result range and pagination | Retain pagination after the tenth listing and before the leaderboard. | Retain reduced mobile page-number display while preserving range, Previous, Next, and current page. | Yes | No | Use JC-011’s `Showing 1–10 of 42` and page sequence. |
| Right rail and support content | Retain the approved JC-010 tablet rail presentation and width; substitute only JC-011 desktop support content. | Stack support content after results, pagination, and leaderboard. | Partial | Yes | The mandated shared mobile sequence conflicts with JC-011’s desktop Current Search, Popular Searches, and Teacher Resources cards. |
| Advertising reservations | Retain the 728×90 leaderboard and 300×250 rail reservation at their governed tablet proportions. | Use responsive leaderboard reservation and centered 300×250 support-flow reservation. | Yes | No | Placement labeling and stable reserved space remain required. |
| Footer | Use the approved JC-010 tablet footer presentation. | Use the approved JC-010 mobile stacked footer presentation. | Yes | No | Presentation inherits; no JC-011-specific footer content is established. |
| Mobile drawer relationship | Not applicable beyond tablet shell behavior. | Use the approved JC-003 logged-out drawer unchanged. | Yes | No | JC-011 may not create a state-specific drawer variant. |

Inherited regions: shell, heading treatment, active search-control layout, results/sort hierarchy, ten-listing narrative treatment, pagination, advertising reservations, footer, and logged-out drawer.

Unique JC-011 responsive deltas:

- Refined-search values, expanded filters, removable applied-filter chips, `42`-result truth, and JC-011’s ten specific listings must come from the JC-011 desktop authority.
- Distance is supported JC-011 listing truth and should remain grouped with salary when present.
- The exact mobile treatment of the already-expanded filter panel needs a JC-011 decision.
- The mobile support-content sequence needs reconciliation with JC-011’s state-specific desktop rail.

Blocker: the Shared Responsive Decisions prescribe `Account → Browse → Employer → Advertisement → Community`, while JC-011 desktop establishes Current Search, Popular Searches, and Teacher Resources. A decision is needed before a JC-011 mobile authority can truthfully inherit the rail.

Recommended scope for JC011-R002: create one tablet and one mobile responsive candidate for the refined-results state, limited to the approved JC-010 presentation language plus JC-011 search/filter/result/listing substitutions; explicitly resolve expanded-filter disclosure and mobile support-rail content/order.

5. **Observation:** The mobile ad strategy is product-suitable. The `320×50` placement between listings 5 and 6 and the `320×100` placement below pagination preserve reading flow and are preferable to compressing desktop leaderboard behavior into mobile.

6. **Implementation:** Control heights, pagination, chip-remove actions, and Save-heart targets appear visually plausible, but implementation must preserve approximately 44px interactive targets without enlarging visible glyphs.

7. **Accessibility:** Browser implementation must verify focus indicators, chip remove names, Sort/select labels, ad labels, and footer/link contrast against WCAG AA.

8. **Design Governance:** The intentional omission of the desktop-derived support-card stack is a governance defect. Shared Responsive Decisions v1 says logged-out Finder/Search right-rail support enters the mobile main flow after results, pagination, and leaderboard in governed order: Account, Browse, Employer, Advertisement, Community.

**Ready for Approval?** No

**Recommendation:** ONE FINAL PATCH REQUIRED

**Rationale:** The candidate is substantially production-ready, and the mobile ad strategy is suitable. Goal

Resolve the governance conflict identified by the JC-011 Mobile production-readiness audit.

Decision

Approve a bounded exception to the ordinary logged-out Finder/Search mobile support-stack rule for JC-011 Mobile only.

Rationale

JC-011 is a refined-results state whose primary task is continued evaluation of search results.

Repeating the full desktop-derived support stack after ten listings would:

- materially lengthen the page
- dilute the search-results task
- duplicate destinations already available through the approved mobile navigation system
- weaken the focused mobile composition

The current JC-011 Mobile candidate preserves State 2 product truth while using task-appropriate mobile advertising and a minimal footer.

Required governance change

## JC-011 Mobile Support-Content Exception

Document that:

- JC-011 Mobile does not inherit the full Account → Browse → Employer → Advertisement → Community support stack.
- After the governed ten listings and pagination, JC-011 Mobile uses:
  1. the approved lower mobile advertisement reservation
  2. the minimal mobile footer
- Account, Browse, Employer, and Community destinations remain available through the approved mobile navigation drawer and are not duplicated below every refined-results page.
- The 320×50 advertisement between listings 5 and 6 and the 320×100 advertisement below pagination are the governed JC-011 Mobile reservations.
- This exception applies only to JC-011 Mobile.
- It does not change JC-010, JC-014, JC-015, JC-030, tablet behavior, desktop behavior, or general support-stack governance.
- Any future exception requires a separate explicit responsive decision.

Update the Visual Manifest and UX Atlas only as needed to cross-reference RESP-DEC002 and record that the current JC-011 Mobile candidate is eligible for approval under this bounded exception.

`720×1950`

A `740px` width cannot preserve the exact aspect ratio because it would require a fractional height: `2004.1667px`.

Source line: 2355

Text:
1. Regions that inherit unchanged

- Shell, navbar, breadcrumb/page heading, search background, listings, right rail/support content, advertisements, footer, typography, spacing rhythm, mobile drawer, and general JC-010 responsive page behavior inherit directly.
- The Location-triggered state inherits JC-010 responsive search structure; only the open modal presentation changes.
- Modal content intent inherits unchanged: Search by location, close control, Current Location / City-State-ZIP / Browse by State tabs, current-location panel, distance control, cross-state checkbox, logged-out sign-in note, Cancel, and Apply.

2. Regions requiring localized responsive adaptation

- Modal width: desktop centered dialog width cannot inherit directly on mobile; it must become an inset viewport-bound dialog.
- Modal height/internal scrolling: desktop height can fit naturally, but mobile must constrain height and scroll the content region internally if needed.
- Viewport positioning: desktop centered overlay cannot simply scale; mobile must preserve surrounding context while remaining reachable in the viewport.
- Tab/action-row presentation: tabs, close control, and bottom actions must remain reachable at narrow widths without wrapping into ambiguity.
- Responsive overflow/dismissal: modal must avoid horizontal overflow and preserve governed dismissal behavior.

3. Responsive deltas, maximum five

1. Mobile modal becomes an inset viewport-bound dialog rather than a scaled desktop-width dialog.
2. Modal maximum height is constrained to the viewport while preserving visible context around the dialog.
3. Modal body/content region scrolls internally when height is constrained; heading, close control, tabs, and bottom action row remain reachable.
4. Tabs retain the same three-option meaning and order but may use mobile-fit spacing so labels remain legible without horizontal overflow.
5. Dismissal behavior remains governed: Cancel, close control, and Escape dismiss without applying; backdrop interaction does not dismiss; focus returns to the Location trigger.

4. Recommended scope for JC014-R002

Produce one JC-014 tablet candidate and one JC-014 mobile candidate by inheriting JC-010 Tablet/Mobile page presentation unchanged, then applying only the localized modal adaptations above. No page redesign, no new modal behavior, and no changes outside the Location modal presentation.

Text:
Product Readiness Audit

- **Design Governance — Conversion hierarchy:** Apply, Save, and Share appear only after all narrative, employer, related-job, and advertisement content. This prevents fast conversion and conflicts with the governed JC-030 mobile priority: Apply → Save → Share → Narrative → Employer → Related Jobs → Advertisement.

- **Observation — Immediate recognition:** Title, employer, location/work arrangement, employment type, salary, chips, and freshness metadata form a clear, calm first-view identity block.

- **Observation — Reading experience:** The larger body copy, generous line-height, section separation, and progressive disclosure provide comfortable sustained reading without visual clutter.

- **Observation — Trust and discovery:** The employer card is appropriately discreet but clear; related-job links are understandable and subordinate; the labeled 320×50 reservation does not interrupt the reading sequence.

Ready for Approval? **No**

Rationale: The design is otherwise visually coherent and supports the intended reading experience, but the primary conversion action is at the page end. One final patch is required: move the existing Apply / Save / Share row to immediately after the job-identity block, retaining its current visual treatment and keeping the remaining content in its existing order.

Source line: 3707
Timestamp: 2026-07-15T15:49:18.978Z

Text:
1. Desktop advertising inventory

- Primary: `728 × 90` leaderboard in the main-content sequence, after the page’s primary task content.
- Secondary: `300 × 250` MPU in the right rail, below task-supporting rail content.
- Hierarchy: primary user task → supporting content → advertisement. Advertising never displaces Apply, search controls, results, or core job evaluation content.

2. Tablet advertising inventory

- Primary tablet banner: `468 × 60`, reserved in the main-content column after the governed primary content.
- Secondary: `300 × 250` MPU remains in the lower right rail when the approved tablet rail is present.
- `728 × 90` is not a tablet main-column reservation while a 300px rail remains visible. It may appear only when a future approved layout provides a full-width post-content reservation of at least 728px without narrowing reading content.

3. Mobile advertising inventory

- `320 × 50` is the standard in-flow mobile reservation.
- `320 × 100` is permitted as a lower, post-pagination reservation for Finder/Search states where explicitly approved.
- Mobile does not inherit desktop/tablet `728 × 90` or `300 × 250` inventory by scaling.
- JC-030 Mobile retains its approved final `320 × 50` location; a lower `320 × 100` is not implied.

4. Placement hierarchy

| Device | Main-flow reservation | Rail / lower reservation |
|---|---|---|
| Desktop | 728×90 after primary content | 300×250 after rail support |
| Portrait tablet | 468×60 after primary main-column content | 300×250 in lower retained rail |
| Mobile | 320×50 at the explicitly approved in-flow break | 320×100 only where expressly approved, after pagination |

5. Permanent responsive layout constraints

- Never compress or distort an advertisement reservation to fit a narrower column.
- A retained tablet right rail must provide a true 300px MPU reservation; if it cannot, the rail must not claim the MPU.
- A 728×90 reservation requires a genuine 728px-wide available placement; it cannot coexist in a narrowed tablet main column merely because it exists on desktop.
- Reserve stable labeled space before inventory loads; no horizontal overflow.
- Advertisements remain below the task’s required action and reading content, never inside a job card, narrative paragraph, or conversion control group.
- Mobile uses only approved mobile banner inventory and locations; no desktop/rail creative is inferred.

6. Recommendation

Create `docs/job-center/job-center-responsive-advertising-strategy-v1.md` as the shared authority. It should codify these device-class inventories, intrinsic-size rules, placement hierarchy, and the exception rule requiring an explicit approval before any screen uses additional or different responsive advertising inventory.

RESP-LAYOUT001 – Responsive Breakpoint and Layout Geometry Review

Follow the Engineering Director Playbook and current Job Center governance.

Read only:

- docs/job-center/job-center-design-system-v1.md
- docs/job-center/job-center-responsive-decisions-v1.md
- docs/job-center/job-center-responsive-advertising-strategy-v1.md, if it already exists

- approved JC-011 desktop, tablet, and mobile authorities
- approved JC-014 desktop, tablet, and mobile authorities
- approved JC-015 desktop, tablet, and mobile authorities
- approved JC-030 desktop and mobile authorities
- current JC-030 tablet candidate

This is a read-only governance review.

Do not generate artwork.
Do not modify documentation.
Do not inspect implementation code.
Do not perform Git activity.

## Goal

Define the responsive layout classes and physical geometry needed to govern future Job Center designs and implementation.

Resolve the current ambiguity around:

- what “tablet” means;
- when a two-column layout is valid;
- minimum main-content width;
- fixed or fluid right-rail width;
- gutters and page insets;
- when the right rail must collapse;
- which advertisement inventories can physically fit.

This review must establish practical geometry rather than preserve unsupported assumptions from prior mockups.

## Required review

Evaluate the following viewport classes:

1. Desktop
2. Wide portrait tablet
3. Narrow portrait tablet
4. Mobile

Landscape tablet may be treated as desktop or wide tablet if justified.

For each class, determine:

- supported viewport-width range;
- preferred design/reference width;
- outer page inset;
- maximum content-shell width;
- column count;
- main-column width or minimum width;
- right-rail width;
- column gap;
- whether the rail is fixed or fluid;
- whether the rail remains visible;
- stacking order when the rail collapses;
- maximum comfortable reading measure.

## Specific questions

Answer explicitly:

1. What is the minimum viewport width at which a true `300px` right rail is permitted?

2. What minimum main-column width must remain beside that rail?

3. What gutter and outer insets are required?

4. At what breakpoint must the two-column tablet layout collapse?

5. When collapsed, what is the governed order of former rail content?

6. Should narrow portrait tablet use:
   - a single-column tablet layout,
   - the mobile layout,
   - or a distinct narrow-tablet class?

7. Which current approved tablet authorities rely on geometry that may not be physically supportable?

Do not invalidate approved authorities. Identify discrepancies as implementation or governance reconciliation items.

## Constraints

Prefer the smallest coherent set of responsive classes.

Do not create device-specific breakpoints for individual screens.

Do not optimize around one mockup.

Do not assume a `300px` rail is valid merely because a placeholder appears in an approved raster.

Do not assume a `728px` banner can scale into a narrower column.

Maintain these priorities:

1. primary task;
2. readable content width;
3. stable layout;
4. support content;
5. advertising.

## Deliverable

Return only:

### 1. Recommended responsive layout classes

Provide a table containing:

| Class | Viewport range | Shell/insets | Main column | Rail | Gap | Layout |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

### 2. Two-column eligibility rule

State the exact minimum geometry required for a retained right rail.

### 3. Rail-collapse rule

State:

- breakpoint;
- resulting layout;
- governed stacking order.

### 4. Reading-width rules

State minimum and preferred reading widths for long-form and listing content.

### 5. Advertising implications

Identify which inventory fits each layout class without yet codifying the full advertising strategy.

### 6. Existing-authority reconciliation

List any approved tablet authorities or current candidates that require implementation notes, Patch Mode review, or future correction because their apparent geometry conflicts with the recommended rules.

### 7. Recommended next ticket

Recommend the scope for:

`RESP-LAYOUT002 – Codify Responsive Layout Geometry v1`

## Stop

Do not update documents.

Do not generate images.

Do not begin JC-030 tablet correction.

Do not perform Git activity.

Stop after the review.

CODEX-019f605b-A0345

Source line: 3774
Timestamp: 2026-07-15T16:47:45.478Z

Text:
### 1. Recommended responsive layout classes

| Class | Viewport range | Shell/insets | Main column | Rail | Gap | Layout |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---:|---|
| Desktop | ≥1200px | 1200px max shell; 32px outer inset | 804px at max shell; readable text capped within it | Fixed 300px, visible | 32px | Two columns |
| Wide portrait tablet | 960–1199px | Fluid shell; 16px outer inset | Minimum 600px; 604px at 960px viewport | Fixed 300px, visible | 24px | Two columns |
| Narrow portrait tablet | 768–959px | Fluid shell; 16px outer inset | Full-width single column | Collapsed below main content | — | Single-column tablet |
| Mobile | <768px | Fluid shell; 16px outer inset | Full-width single column | Not persistent; governed support content stacks | — | Mobile layout |

Landscape tablet uses Wide Portrait Tablet rules when its viewport width is at least 960px; otherwise it uses Narrow Portrait Tablet rules.

### 2. Two-column eligibility rule

A retained true 300px right rail requires all of:

- Viewport width of at least 960px.
- 16px minimum outer inset on both sides.
- Fixed 300px rail.
- 24px column gap.
- Main column of at least 600px.

Minimum physical geometry: `16 + 600 + 24 + 300 + 16 = 956px`; 960px is the practical breakpoint floor.

### 3. Rail-collapse rule

- Breakpoint: below 960px, or whenever the main column would fall below 600px.
- Result: Narrow Portrait Tablet single-column layout; do not compress the main column or shrink a nominal 300px rail.
- Finder/Search stacking order: primary content → pagination → main-flow advertisement → Account → Browse → Employer → 300×250 advertisement → Community.
- JC-030 follows its governed Job Detail sequence rather than the Finder support stack: primary job content → Employer → Related Jobs → advertisement.

### 4. Reading-width rules

- Two-column long-form content: 600px minimum; 640–720px preferred reading measure.
- Two-column listing content: 600px minimum; 640–800px preferred.
- Single-column narrow-tablet content: fluid, with long-form text capped near 720px where practical.
- Mobile content: fluid within 16px insets; preserve a minimum practical content width of 320px rather than reducing typography or controls.

### 5. Advertising implications

- Desktop: 728×90 main-flow reservation and 300×250 right-rail reservation.
- Wide portrait tablet: 468×60 main-flow reservation and true 300×250 right-rail reservation.
- Narrow portrait tablet: 468×60 main-flow reservation; 300×250 may appear only after the collapsed support content at its intrinsic width.
- Mobile: 320×50; 320×100 only where explicitly approved, including JC-011’s post-pagination exception. A fixed 320px creative requires at least a 352px viewport with 16px side insets; never scale it down automatically.
- A 728px banner cannot occupy a narrowed main column beside a retained 300px rail.

### 6. Existing-authority reconciliation

- JC-010 and JC-011 tablet authorities are valid Wide Portrait Tablet reference authorities at their approximately 962–963px reference widths. Their apparent 728×90 main-column reservations require implementation reconciliation to the governed 468×60 tablet inventory when a 300px rail remains visible.
- JC-014 and JC-015 tablet authorities inherit the same JC-010 tablet shell geometry; their retained-rail behavior applies only at Wide Portrait Tablet widths.
- None of the approved tablet authorities establishes a two-column rule below 960px. Narrow portrait tablet behavior needs explicit governance rather than extrapolation.
- The current JC-030 tablet candidate is not physically supportable as shown: its approximately 864px canvas retains a desktop-style two-column layout and 728×90 main-column reservation. It requires correction before approval, including the already noted tablet-footer alignment issue.
- These are reconciliation and Patch Mode items; they do not invalidate existing approvals.

### 7. Recommended next ticket

`RESP-LAYOUT002 – Codify Responsive Layout Geometry v1` should document only:

- the four layout classes and breakpoint thresholds;
- the 960px two-column eligibility formula;
- fixed 300px rail, 24px tablet gap, and required insets;
- narrow-tablet collapse and screen-specific stacking exceptions;
- reading-width rules;
- intrinsic advertising-fit constraints;
- reconciliation notes for existing approved tablet authorities and the unapproved JC-030 tablet candidate.

It should not alter approved rasters, authorize implementation, or begin the JC-030 tablet correction.

Timestamp: 2026-07-18T09:25:34.659Z

Text:
There’s no fixed schedule. For a project like Teachers.Net, I’d keep one chat active for a coherent workstream and start a new chat at a natural boundary:

- After a major milestone or handoff.
- When the task changes from implementation to audit, documentation, or a different product area.
- When responses become noticeably slower, repetitive, or confused.
- When the conversation has accumulated substantial logs, images, or tool output.
- When switching from Job Center to Core Terms or Membership Taxonomy.

As a practical rule: one chat per focused workstream for roughly a day or a few major tasks, then begin a fresh chat with a short continuity instruction. Don’t start new chats merely because the thread is old; durable project docs and a concise handoff are more valuable than frequent resets.

For your current Job Center work, I would start a new chat after Employer Operations desktop visual acceptance, using the updated Project Cursor and Engineering Handoff as the recovery anchor. Codex examples also support sustained review within one thread when the work remains coherent. [OpenAI Codex use cases](https://developers.openai.com/codex/use-cases)

CODEX-019f7481-A0010
Role: ASSISTANT
Source line: 143
Timestamp: 2026-07-18T09:27:18.257Z

Text:
Usually, yes—but not perfectly.

A new chat can regain continuity if you instruct Codex to:

> Review the prior chat as historical context, then verify current state against the project’s Project Cursor, Engineering Handoff, and repository.

That gives you a cleaner active context and often better responsiveness. It does not guarantee zero information loss: exact wording, minor decisions, rejected alternatives, and tool outputs may not all be retained or retrievable.

For reliable continuity, the best sequence is:

1. Finish the old chat with a concise handoff.
2. Update the project’s Cursor/Handoff if durable state changed.
3. Start the new chat with the prior-chat review instruction.
4. Tell Codex which current repository documents are authoritative.

For this project:

> Review “Job Center 7/15/26” as historical context. Then read `docs/job-center/project-cursor.md` and `docs/job-center/engineering-handoff.md`, verify the current repository state, identify stale assumptions or conflicts, and report readiness before taking action.

This usually provides the benefits of a fresh working context, but reading a large prior chat can temporarily add work. A concise handoff is faster and more reliable than asking Codex to ingest the entire prior conversation.

  `\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu-24.04\home\bobreap\projects\teachers-net-site`
- Therefore, `sandboxCwd` does not need to match the repository for basic JS execution.
- The current Codex-managed MCP config does not define a Windows-local cwd:
  `[mcp_servers.node_repl] args = []`

- JS with neutral Windows cwd: PASS in a standalone MCP subprocess.
- Browser-client setup with `--disable-sandbox` plus explicit Codex turn metadata: PARTIAL.

Text:
TOOL-DIAG008 — External Chrome CDP Feasibility Study

Objective

Determine whether Codex Desktop can use an external Windows Chrome instance through Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) for authenticated browser QA, bypassing the failing built-in browser sandbox.

Known issue

The built-in browser runtime starts successfully but fails because Codex passes a WSL thread cwd as:

file:///home/...

The Windows sandbox rejects that value as a non-local file URI before browser navigation begins.

Scope

Perform a read-only feasibility study. Do not modify project files, repository state, DDEV, WSL configuration, Chrome’s normal profile, or Codex project metadata.

Investigate

1. Whether Codex Desktop supports adding and invoking an external Chrome DevTools MCP server.
2. Whether the installed Codex configuration supports a custom MCP entry for chrome-devtools-mcp or equivalent.
3. Whether Windows Chrome can be launched with:
   - a dedicated QA profile
   - localhost-only remote debugging
   - a fixed debugging port
4. Whether WSL and the Codex app-server can reach the CDP endpoint.
5. Whether the external browser path bypasses sandboxCwd validation entirely.
6. Whether the MCP can perform:
   - page navigation
   - authenticated-session reuse
   - screenshot capture
   - DOM inspection
   - console inspection
   - page-error inspection
   - viewport measurement
   - horizontal-overflow measurement
   - click/type interaction
7. Whether this can coexist safely with the existing built-in browser-control configuration.
8. Whether enabling it requires:
   - editing config.toml
   - installing an MCP package
   - restarting Codex Desktop
   - creating a new task/thread
9. Security implications:
   - bind address
   - port exposure
   - dedicated profile isolation
   - access to unrelated browser data
10. Maintenance implications:
   - startup procedure
   - version dependencies
   - update risk
   - impact on other Codex projects

Preferred test architecture

Codex Desktop
→ external Chrome DevTools MCP
→ dedicated Windows Chrome QA profile
→ https://teachers-net.ddev.site/

Constraints

Do not:

- move or copy the repository
- alter Git history
- alter DDEV
- alter WSL
- edit Codex state databases
- use the normal personal Chrome profile
- expose the debugging port beyond localhost
- install or modify anything until the required changes are listed and approved
- restart Codex during this feasibility study

Deliver

Report:

- FEASIBLE, FEASIBLE WITH CONDITIONS, or NOT FEASIBLE
- exact required components
- exact configuration changes
- whether a Codex restart is required
- whether a new thread/project is required
- expected one-time setup cost
- expected recurring operator cost
- security risks and mitigations
- impact on existing projects
- whether it bypasses the verified sandboxCwd defect
- recommended implementation plan
- rollback procedure

Verification standard

Distinguish verified facts from assumptions. Cite concrete executable paths, configuration keys, commands, and observed endpoint behavior where available.

Do not implement. Stop after the feasibility report.

Text:
FEASIBLE WITH CONDITIONS.

Codex Desktop can plausibly use an external Windows Chrome instance via Chrome DevTools Protocol and a custom MCP server, bypassing the verified `sandboxCwd` defect. I did not implement or modify anything.

Verified facts:

- Codex supports external MCP server config:
  - Local CLI exposes `codex mcp add <NAME> -- <COMMAND>...`
  - Existing config already uses `[mcp_servers.node_repl]`, so TOML MCP entries are supported.
- `chrome-devtools-mcp` exists on npm:
  - package: `chrome-devtools-mcp`
  - version observed: `1.6.0`
  - CLI bin: `chrome-devtools-mcp`
  - supports `--browser-url=http://127.0.0.1:9222`
- Its published tool list includes:
  - navigation
  - screenshots
  - DOM/snapshot inspection
  - console message inspection
  - script evaluation
  - viewport resize/emulation
  - click/type/fill interaction
  - network inspection
- Windows Chrome is installed:
  - `C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe`
  - version observed: `150.0.7871.128`
- Windows can reach the DDEV route:
  - `https://teachers-net.ddev.site/jobs/employer/my-jobs/`
  - HEAD returned `200 OK`
- No CDP endpoint is currently open on `127.0.0.1:9222`.
- Current Codex tool surface does not yet expose a `chrome-devtools` MCP namespace.

Required components:

1. Dedicated Windows Chrome QA profile.
2. Chrome launched with localhost-only CDP.
3. `chrome-devtools-mcp` MCP server.
4. Codex MCP config entry pointing at that CDP endpoint.

Proposed Chrome launch command:

```powershell
& "C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe" `
  --user-data-dir="$env:LOCALAPPDATA\CodexChromeQA\TeachersNet" `
  --remote-debugging-address=127.0.0.1 `
  --remote-debugging-port=9222 `
  --new-window "https://teachers-net.ddev.site/"
```

Proposed Codex config entry:

```toml
[mcp_servers.chrome-devtools]
command = "cmd"
args = [
  "/c",
  "npx",
  "-y",
  "chrome-devtools-mcp@1.6.0",
  "--browser-url=http://127.0.0.1:9222",
  "--no-usage-statistics"
]
env = { SystemRoot = "C:\\Windows", PROGRAMFILES = "C:\\Program Files" }
```

Whether it bypasses `sandboxCwd`:
- Expected yes.
- Reason: this path would use an independent MCP server that talks to Chrome over HTTP/CDP. It should not depend on Codex’s built-in `node_repl` browser sandbox metadata.
- Not yet proven because the MCP was not installed/configured/launched.

Authentication:
- It should not use the normal personal Chrome profile.
- First run with the dedicated QA profile will likely require manual login.
- After login, the dedicated profile should retain the authenticated session across QA runs.

Codex restart required:
- Likely yes, or at least an MCP reload.
- Verified: Codex CLI supports adding MCP servers.
- Not verified: Codex Desktop hot-reloads new MCP config in an already-running task.
- Lowest-risk assumption: config change + Codex Desktop restart, unless a reload command is found.

New thread/project required:
- No evidence that a new task or project is required.
- This should coexist with the current Teachers.Net project because it is an additional MCP server, not a workspace rebind.

Expected one-time setup cost:
- 10–20 minutes:
  - add MCP config
  - launch dedicated Chrome QA profile
  - authenticate once
  - restart/reload Codex if needed
  - run smoke test

Expected recurring operator cost:
- Low:
  - start Chrome QA profile with the CDP command
  - confirm port `9222` is open
  - run browser QA through the `chrome-devtools` MCP tools

Security risks and mitigations:
- Risk: CDP allows full inspection/control of that browser instance.
  - Mitigation: dedicated QA profile only.
- Risk: exposing CDP beyond localhost.
  - Mitigation: bind `--remote-debugging-address=127.0.0.1`.
- Risk: MCP can inspect authenticated app data.
  - Mitigation: use only Teachers.Net QA profile, not personal Chrome.
- Risk: npm `@latest` update drift.
  - Mitigation: pin `chrome-devtools-mcp@1.6.0` initially.

Impact on existing projects:
- Should be additive.
- Existing built-in browser-control config can remain unchanged.
- Other projects could reuse the MCP if Chrome QA profile/port is running, but session data would be shared unless separate profiles/ports are used.

Recommended implementation plan:

1. Add the `[mcp_servers.chrome-devtools]` entry pinned to `chrome-devtools-mcp@1.6.0`.
2. Restart or reload Codex MCPs if required.
3. Launch dedicated Windows Chrome QA profile on `127.0.0.1:9222`.
4. Authenticate Teachers.Net once in that QA profile.
5. Run smoke test:
   - navigate to All My Jobs
   - screenshot
   - DOM snapshot
   - viewport resize to 1440px
   - console messages
   - page errors via script/listeners where supported
   - horizontal overflow measurement via `evaluate_script`
6. If successful, document the startup command in the smallest local workflow note.

Rollback procedure:

1. Close the dedicated QA Chrome window.
2. Remove `[mcp_servers.chrome-devtools]` from Codex config.
3. Restart/reload Codex MCPs if needed.
4. Optionally delete the dedicated QA profile directory:
   - `C:\Users\bobre\AppData\Local\CodexChromeQA\TeachersNet`

Bottom line: this is the most promising workaround so far. It targets the failure cleanly because the current defect is inside Codex’s built-in browser sandbox metadata path, while CDP uses an already-running external Chrome over localhost.

EMP-PATCH012 — Lifecycle Filter and State Display Convergence

Objective

Use the completed `jobman` lifecycle fixture matrix to correct filter behavior, filtered counts, and state-specific timeline presentation across every supported visible employer-job branch.

Authority

- Existing lifecycle/state logic remains authoritative.
- `docs/employer-lifecycle-fixture-matrix.md` is the canonical QA matrix.
- Use the seeded `jobman` lifecycle fixtures.
- Use only external `chrome-devtools` MCP for authenticated browser verification.

Route

https://teachers-net.ddev.site/jobs/employer/my-jobs/

Phase 1 — Filter default and reset behavior

Default state:

- show all manageable jobs
- no specific lifecycle filter active
- do not show an `All` chip

When any specific filter is selected:

- activate only that filter
- add an `All` chip at the far right of the filter row
- clicking `All` clears the filter and returns to the default unfiltered state
- remove the `All` chip again after reset
- keep all existing lifecycle chips stationary; `All` must appear last so other controls do not shift

Preserve query-string, reload, back/forward, keyboard, and focus behavior.

Phase 2 — Filter totals and pagination consistency

Correct the known defect for filtered views.

For every selected filter:

- hero job count must reflect the filtered result set
- pagination summary must reflect the filtered result set
- page count must derive from the filtered result set
- rows-per-page behavior must operate on the filtered set
- empty-result state must report zero accurately
- do not show unfiltered totals while displaying filtered rows

Verify at minimum:

- Draft
- Awaiting Review
- Live
- Expiring Soon
- Expired
- Closed
- All/default

Phase 3 — Canonical state-specific timeline rendering

Implement the canonical expected output documented in the lifecycle fixture matrix for every supported visible branch.

At minimum cover:

- Draft
- Submitted / Awaiting Review
- Approved stored, if visibly distinct
- Live healthy
- Live expiring soon
- Expired by date
- Expired materialized
- Closed
- Renewed draft
- Duplicate draft

For each branch verify:

- exact line-one wording
- exact line-two wording
- exact line-three wording
- semantic text colors
- bullet color
- black date text where specified
- primary action
- overflow actions

Requirements:

- use actual stored/derived dates
- do not invent timestamps
- do not change lifecycle derivation
- do not collapse distinct states merely for visual convenience
- preserve archived as intentionally hidden
- preserve EMP-PATCH011 LIVE formatting unless the fixture matrix requires a correction

Phase 4 — Fixture-driven browser verification

Use the existing commands:

ddev wp tnet-jobs recruiter-ux-fixture lifecycle_create --allow-root
ddev wp tnet-jobs recruiter-ux-fixture lifecycle_verify --allow-root
ddev wp tnet-jobs recruiter-ux-fixture lifecycle_status --allow-root

- default route shows all jobs with no `All` chip
- each lifecycle filter shows only expected fixtures
- `All` appears last only while a specific filter is active
- clicking `All` restores the unfiltered state
- hero count is correct
- pagination summary is correct
- rows-per-page is correct
- state wording and semantic colors match the matrix
- primary and overflow actions match the matrix
- archived fixture remains hidden
- no horizontal overflow
- no clipped content
- console errors: 0
- page errors: 0

Constraints

- change lifecycle semantics
- change moderation or trust rules
- alter fixture definitions unless a verified fixture defect requires it
- expose archived jobs
- add unsupported states
- redesign the table or workspace
- modify unrelated files
- clean root-repository dirty files

Text:
EMP-DES001 — Approved-State Employer Workspace Decision

Objective

Resolve the remaining product ambiguity around jobs stored as `approved` before any further Employer Workspace visual work.

Known state

- `approved` jobs appear in the default All My Jobs view.
- They have no dedicated filter.
- The fixture matrix labels this an unsupported workspace branch.
- Current rendering exposes:
  `Approved • Expires [date]`
- It is unclear whether `approved` is:
  - a transient internal moderation state,
  - an employer-visible lifecycle state,
  - or a state that should immediately transition to `published`.

Scope

Audit the real lifecycle path for `submitted → approved → published`.

Determine:

1. Who or what sets `approved`.
2. Whether publication normally follows automatically.
3. Whether an approved job can remain stranded indefinitely.
4. Whether employers should ever see an approved-only row.
5. Whether approved jobs belong in:
   - All My Jobs,
   - Awaiting Review,
   - Live,
   - or no employer-visible list.
6. Appropriate timeline wording and primary/overflow actions if approved remains visible.
7. Recovery behavior for existing approved records.
8. Whether the fixture should remain, change expectation, or become a negative/invariant test.

Use

- existing services, repositories, moderation logic, and docs
- `docs/employer-lifecycle-fixture-matrix.md`
- the seeded `[QA STATE] Approved Stored` fixture
- authenticated external Chrome DevTools where useful

Deliver

- verified lifecycle trace
- stored versus intended behavior
- explicit product recommendation
- smallest implementation plan
- data-migration/backfill requirement, if any
- fixture-matrix update required
- proposed next implementation ticket

Constraints

Do not:

- change code
- change job records
- change lifecycle semantics
- modify fixtures
- implement UI
- infer intent without tracing actual behavior
- touch unrelated files

Git

Documentation-only commit only if an authoritative decision record is added or updated.

Stop after the decision and implementation recommendation.

Text:
EMP-DES001 audit complete. No files changed, no commit.

Decision recommendation: treat stored `approved` as an internal/transitional admin/import artifact, not an employer-visible lifecycle state. Approval should resolve immediately to `published` when the job is publishable. Employers should not see an approved-only row.

Verified lifecycle trace:

- Employer-created jobs become either:
  - `submitted` for standard-review employers
  - `published` for trusted employers, with `approved_at` and `published_at` set.
- Moderation approval only accepts `submitted` jobs and writes:
  - `status = published`
  - `approved_at = now`
  - `published_at = now`
- Admin notices and events call the result “approved and published.”
- Recruiter lifecycle email logic treats `submitted → published` as the approval event.
- Employer edit access excludes `approved`; approved-only records are not editable by employers.
- Employer row actions also exclude `approved` from edit/duplicate/close/renew, leaving only the fallback View action.

Stored vs intended behavior:

- Stored behavior: `approved` is an allowed status and can be created/updated through admin/programmatic paths.
- Intended behavior, based on actual moderation/trust flow: approved means “approval happened,” but the employer-visible lifecycle result is `published`.
- Current leak: All My Jobs default query includes `approved` because it includes all non-archived manageable jobs unless a filter is selected.
- Local DB check: only one approved record exists, and it is the `[QA STATE] Approved Stored` fixture. Zero non-fixture approved records.

Answers to the eight questions:

1. Who sets `approved`?
   - Normal moderation does not. Admin job create/edit or programmatic service calls can set it because it remains an allowed stored status.

2. Does publication normally follow automatically?
   - Yes. The real moderation approval path writes `published`, not `approved`.

3. Can approved remain stranded indefinitely?
   - Yes, if created/updated through admin generic job editing, imports, fixtures, or direct service calls.

4. Should employers ever see approved-only rows?
   - Recommendation: no.

5. Approved jobs belong in:
   - All My Jobs: no
   - Awaiting Review: no
   - Live: no, unless converted to `published`
   - No employer-visible list: yes, pending recovery/invariant handling

6. If approved remains visible, wording/actions?
   - Recommendation: do not keep visible. If temporarily exposed for diagnostics only: “Pending publication” with no employer mutation actions. But this should not be product UI.

7. Recovery behavior for existing approved records:
   - Backfill approved records to `published` when:
     - `archived_at IS NULL`
     - not expired
     - `approved_at` exists or can be set
     - publication eligibility is otherwise valid
   - Set `published_at` from `approved_at` when available, otherwise `updated_at`/current time under a migration note.
   - If expired, archived, missing required publication fields, or suppressed, do not blindly publish; route to admin review or leave hidden.

8. Fixture matrix:
   - Convert `approved_stored` from a visible matrix branch into a negative/invariant test: approved-only records must not appear in employer workspace views.
   - Keep the fixture only if it verifies the invariant; otherwise remove it from visible branch coverage.

Smallest implementation plan:

1. Repository/workspace visibility:
   - Exclude `status = approved` from Employer Operations manageable job lists.

2. Admin lifecycle normalization:
   - Remove `approved` from generic admin create/edit status dropdowns, or normalize admin-selected `approved` to `published` through the same approval helper.

3. Backfill:
   - Add a guarded migration/CLI command for existing approved records.
   - In local DDEV, expected non-fixture migration count is currently 0.

4. Fixture update:
   - Update EMP-QA002 matrix so `[QA STATE] Approved Stored` is hidden and verified as an invariant.

Proposed next implementation ticket:

`EMP-IMP013 — Approved-State Invariant and Recovery`

Scope:

- Hide approved-only jobs from Employer Operations.
- Prevent new stranded approved records through admin create/edit.
- Add guarded approved→published recovery for eligible records.
- Convert the approved fixture to a hidden invariant test.
- Verify no approved-only row appears in All My Jobs or filters.

No unresolved lifecycle display decision remains for visual work, as long as `approved` is treated as non-employer-visible and transitional/internal.

DESIGN-FOUNDATION001 complete. No repository files were modified and no commit was made.

Result: the current production stack already renders as Segoe UI in the Windows Chrome QA profile. Explicit Segoe UI injection produced no measurable layout or wrapping difference. The remaining JC-050 typography drift is therefore not primarily a font-family problem; it is more likely weight/scale/line-height/token tuning.

### Current production stack

Computed production stack across sampled areas:

`-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif`

On this Windows Chrome QA path, canvas measurement confirms the effective rendered family is Segoe UI.

### Baseline computed typography

| Area | Size | Weight | Line height | Letter spacing |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Navbar | 16px | 300 | 24px | normal |
| Page heading | 24.8px | 800 | 26.784px | -0.1px |
| Rail heading | 11.52px | 800 | 17.28px | 0.4608px |
| Selected rail card | 16px | 300 | 24px | normal |
| Filter chips | 11.52px | 700 | 12.672px | normal |
| Table headers | 11.2px | 800 | 12.32px | 0.112px |
| Job titles | 14.4px | 800 | 16.56px | -0.144px |
| School/site text | 12.16px | 400 | 13.984px | normal |
| Timeline primary | 12.8px | 800 | 14.72px | normal |
| Timeline date text | 12.8px | 800 | 14.72px | normal |
| Action buttons | 11.84px | 800 | 14.208px | normal |
| Metadata | 11.2px | 300 | 12.88px | normal |

### Candidate availability

| Candidate | Available locally by canvas proof | Tested |
|---|---:|---:|
| Current production stack | Yes | Yes |
| Segoe UI | Yes | Yes |
| Inter | No; resolved to fallback | No |
| Source Sans 3 | No; resolved to fallback | No |
| Roboto | No; resolved to fallback | No |
| Noto Sans | No; resolved to fallback | No |
| IBM Plex Sans | No; resolved to fallback | No |

Note: `document.fonts.check()` returned true for several unavailable families, but canvas-width comparison showed they rendered identically to the missing-font fallback. I treated canvas proof as authoritative.

### Measured comparison

| Metric | Current stack | Explicit Segoe UI | Difference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Viewport | 1440×1000 | 1440×1000 | none |
| Document height | 1639px | 1639px | 0 |
| Horizontal overflow | No | No | none |
| Selected rail-card height | 58.1px | 58.1px | 0 |
| Hero-to-toolbar spacing | 18px | 18px | 0 |
| Toolbar-to-table spacing | 18px | 18px | 0 |
| Inventory row range | 80–82.6px | 80–82.6px | 0 |
| Action button | 70.4×28px | 70.4×28px | 0 |
| Title wrapping distribution | unchanged | unchanged | 0 |

Screenshots were captured inline for:

- current production stack
- explicit Segoe UI injection

Saving screenshots to file hit the known WSL/Windows path translation issue in the DevTools MCP, so I kept them inline and restored the page afterward.

### Ranking

1. Current production stack / Segoe UI — best verified match, zero loading cost, no layout risk.
2. Inter — plausible visual alternative, but not locally available; would require a webfont dependency to evaluate honestly.
3. Source Sans 3 — not locally available; likely softer/wider, unproven.
4. Roboto — not locally available; would add loading dependency and likely shifts character rhythm.
5. Noto Sans — not locally available; broad fallback value, but not a JC-050 match candidate here.
6. IBM Plex Sans — not locally available; likely too distinctive for this UI.

### Recommendation

Keep the production system stack, but make it canonical and explicit for Job Center:

```css
-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif
```

Use only:

- regular: 400
- bold: 700

Current usage includes 300 and 800 in several places. The visual drift against JC-050 is more likely from those heavier/lighter weights and local sizing than from the family itself.

### Proposed implementation ticket

`DESIGN-IMP001 — JC-050 Typography Token Weight Convergence`

Scope:

- keep the current system font stack;
- normalize Job Center typography tokens toward 400/700;
- reduce reliance on 300 and 800 where JC-050 calls for ordinary regular/bold hierarchy;
- do not change layout, colors, lifecycle, or data behavior;
- verify at 1440×1000 with external Chrome DevTools.

- console errors: 0
- page errors: 0

Diagnosis complete. No images or repository files were modified.

Confirmed geometry:

| Artifact | Canvas | Card bounds | Rail | Main workspace |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| `final.png` | 1220×915 | x=10–1209, y=5–904 | 250px | 950px |
| `final-clean.png` | 1220×915 | x=10–1209, y=5–904 | 250px | 950px |
| Approved v1.1 reference | 1333×1180 | larger framed composition | not directly comparable | not directly comparable |

Root cause:

1. The card has only 10px of right canvas space.
2. The intended shadow spread exceeds that available space, so the right shadow is clipped at the canvas boundary.
3. The bottom shadow is similarly constrained by the 10px bottom space.
4. The protected 1200×900 mask includes the malformed source-side edge, preventing the cleanup pass from rebuilding it.
5. The cleanup pass changed only outside the protected region, so it could remove exterior artifacts but could not correct the defective edge pixels embedded in the locked card raster.
6. The card is geometrically centered only by the nominal 10px margins; it is not centered relative to the required shadow envelope.

The two prior passes failed because they preserved the defective card raster and attempted to repair the surrounding pixels without first creating enough canvas for the full shadow geometry.

Recommended repair: option B plus option E

Re-center the unchanged 1200×900 application raster inside a slightly wider reconstructed card frame.

Proposed geometry:

- Canvas: 1228×919 px
- Card: x=14–1213, y=5–904
- Card interior: exactly 1200×900 px
- Rail: 250px
- Main workspace: 950px
- Left/right page margins: 14px
- Top/bottom page margins: 5px / 14px
- Card radius: 12px
- Border: 1px continuous border
- Shadow: symmetric 14px maximum spread, soft opacity, no clipping

Method:

- Reposition the locked application raster by +4px horizontally.
- Reconstruct the complete outer card mask and shadow outside the protected raster.
- Keep the logo and all application pixels byte-identical after translation.
- Validate with a translation-aware pixel comparison rather than a same-coordinate comparison.
- Inspect all four corners and the full right edge at 100%, 200%, and 400%.

Options rejected:

- A: Extending only the right canvas leaves asymmetric framing.
- C: Rebuilding only the right edge risks visible seams.
- D: Mirroring left geometry alone does not solve the clipped shadow envelope.
- Full global scaling is prohibited and unnecessary.

Confidence: high.

The current artifact should not replace the authority yet. A new narrowly scoped raster-reframe ticket should authorize the wider canvas and translation-aware protected-pixel verification.

NAV-DIAG002 — Navbar Separation Rendering and Cascade Diagnosis

Objective

- box-shadow: 0 3px 8px rgba(32, 45, 68, 0.08)

1. CASCADE AUDIT
==========================================================

Inspect every rule affecting:

- the workspace immediately below the navbar

- selector

- specificity

- whether `!important` is used

Determine why `!important` was introduced and whether the underlying conflict can be removed.

==========================================================

Use DevTools to test whether the shadow is:

- clipped by ancestor overflow
- hidden beneath another stacking context
- painted behind the workspace
- visually lost against the adjacent background
- too low-opacity to match the authority

- obscured by a later element

Inspect:

- stacking contexts

Temporarily exaggerate the shadow in DevTools only to establish whether it can render visibly from the current element.

3. MAINTAINABLE FIX
==========================================================

Implement the smallest coherent fix only after identifying the cause.

Preferred outcomes:

- remove the need for `!important`

- apply the border/shadow to the correct visual boundary

Do not solve the problem by:
